n14fd18d5d69d: Cohesin is a ring-shaped protein complex that wraps around DNA and is crucial for sister chromatid cohesion, chromatin organization, gene regulation, replication, and DNA damage repair. In somatic cells, it consists of the core ring subunits SMC1A, SMC3, and RAD21 and one of two paralogs, STAG1 or STAG2. Germline mutations in the cohesin ring and its loading complex components cause developmental disorders such as Cornelia de Lange and Roberts syndromes, collectively referred to as cohesinopathies. Similar loss-of-function mutations in cohesin are somatically acquired during cancer development and are prevalent across multiple cancer types, particularly myeloid malignancies, bladder cancer, glioblastoma, and Ewing sarcoma. Here, we discuss the context-dependent effects of cohesin mutations in development and cancer and describe their underlying molecular mechanisms. A deeper understanding of cohesin function in normal development and human disease holds promise to identify new therapeutic opportunities for patients with cohesin dysfunction.
ne444ff844cd1: The inability to restrict acute myeloid leukemia immunotherapy to leukemic cells without damaging normal hematopoiesis remains a central challenge. Graft engineering addresses this limitation by modifying donor hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells so that the reconstituting hematopoietic system becomes resistant to a selected immunotherapy while residual leukemia remains susceptible. I examine the molecular principles, target-specific constraints, pharmacological consequences, and translational implications of this strategy across five validated immunotargets: CD33, CD123, FLT3, KIT, and CD45. These targets span a spectrum from dispensable lineage antigens to essential signaling receptors and pan-hematopoietic conditioning targets, requiring either antigen deletion or function-preserving epitope substitution. Beyond preventing hematopoietic toxicity, graft engineering redistributes therapeutic engagement by remodeling normal antigen-expressing hematopoiesis, thereby influencing the efficacy and toxicity of antibody- and chimeric antigen receptor–based therapies. I outline a translational path from single-edited grafts toward multiplex platforms designed to improve disease control while limiting antigen escape.
nfdeaeb110ca0: Metabolic reprogramming supports cancer behaviors including proliferation, survival, and therapeutic resistance. Compared to our understanding of these processes, little is known about the detoxification liabilities that are introduced as a byproduct of this reprogramming. Here, we review recent findings that collectively support the notion that the metabolic reprogramming of cancer cells is accompanied by increased production of potentially toxic metabolites. As a result, these cells are critically dependent on enzymatic processing or export of these metabolites. When such processes are blocked, endogenously produced metabolites can accumulate in distinct subcellular compartments to exert a variety of cytotoxic mechanisms in cancer cells such as DNA damage and ferroptosis. Toxic metabolite overloading is discussed as an emerging therapeutic strategy that carries potential advantages such as allowing tuning of toxicity via dietary control of metabolite production and exerting microenvironmental toxic effects to enhance overall efficacy in the heterogenous tumor.
n46b5cb4ad4a9: This review traces the evolution of the specialization concept in criminology and assesses its value for theory, research, and policy. Although empirical research has generally shown that most offenders exhibit versatility rather than long-term specialization, we argue that specialization remains an important dimension of criminal behavior and is productive for middle-range theory and normal science in criminology. We assess common methodological approaches to measuring specialization, highlighting how differences in operationalization shape substantive conclusions. We then synthesize contemporary research that uses specialization to probe theoretical mechanisms, examine social and developmental processes, and evaluate justice system practices and policy. Across these areas, between- and within-individual variation in specialization (versatility) informs questions about opportunity, peer influence, decision-making, and the criminal career. We conclude that specialization should not be treated as a binary property but as a conditional, theoretically generative construct that, if effectively utilized, can advance criminology's objectives.
nddb5891a4eff: As classic examples of adaptive evolution, insect mimicry and masquerade have been studied extensively for more than a century. Both phenomena protect insects from predators and are widely observed in nature. Previous research on phenotypic, genetic, phylogenetic, and behavioral aspects has laid a solid foundation for in-depth investigations. Recent advances in genomic data resources, analytical methodologies, and gene-editing tools have greatly facilitated the elucidation of the genetic and developmental mechanisms underlying insect mimicry and masquerade. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent progress, encompassing key insect lineages such as Lepidoptera, Hymenoptera, Odonata, and Mantodea; highlights the pivotal roles of evolutionary hot spot genes, noncoding sequences, and structural variations in driving phenotypic diversification and adaptation; and offers novel insights into fundamental evolutionary questions such as sexual dimorphism, convergent evolution, and speciation. Furthermore, this review outlines the ongoing challenges and future prospects in the evolutionary genetics of insect mimicry and masquerade.
n3b135b4079f5: Sign language machine translation has progressed substantially over the past decade, evolving from isolated sign recognition to end-to-end translation systems. Advances in pose estimation, transformer architectures, and large-scale dataset collection have driven progress, yet challenges remain. Datasets are limited compared to spoken-language resources; evaluation metrics inadequately capture the linguistic quality of output; and models must capture the simultaneous, multilayered, and three-dimensional structure of sign languages. This manuscript provides a comprehensive review that seeks to balance technical challenges with stakeholder considerations. We examine the linguistic properties that make sign languages computationally unique; trace the evolution of recognition, translation, and production systems; and analyze ongoing technical challenges. Crucially, we address ethical considerations around data governance, community involvement, and appropriate use. Drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives spanning computer vision, sign language linguistics, and deaf studies, our analysis emphasizes that continued progress requires sustained collaboration across these fields and with deaf communities.
ncba416a50cc7: The tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) has emerged as a crucial regulator of antitumor immune responses with important therapeutic, prognostic, and predictive implications. Despite the success of immunotherapies in select solid tumors, notably melanoma and non–small cell lung cancer, their impact in soft-tissue sarcomas (STSs) is limited, often attributed to an immune-cold TIME passively driven by low neoantigen burden. Herein, we review the current understanding of the STS TIME, its variability across STS subtypes, and its implications for STS immunotherapy. We propose that the prevailing view of STSs as passively immune-cold is incomplete and that active tumor-driven immune suppression is likely underappreciated. Distinguishing active from passive immune escape and understanding its mechanistic underpinnings will be important to rationally design effective TIME-targeted therapies in STSs and to serve as a paradigm for therapeutic interventions in other immune-cold tumors.
n17c07594ee10: My professional life owes a great deal to the popular attitudes about science during my youth. As member of the baby boom generation, I benefited from a national commitment to the progress of science and the creation of institutions to support research. The path that took me into science and a career in fundamental research and, finally, into government service reflects those influences on the research enterprise. I encountered inspiring mentors along the way and eventually began independent research at the University of Wisconsin, exploring vibrations in chemical reactions. Studies of vibrationally excited molecules led from collisional energy transfer to unimolecular reactions, to photodissociation, and to bimolecular reactions. The photodissociation and bimolecular reaction experiments were among the first to demonstrate vibrational-state control of a reaction. Along the way, we did spectroscopy to explore vibrational excitation in polyatomic molecules and worked to recapitulate gas-phase studies in liquids.
nf93c70f0f405: The methylidyne radical, CH, can react rapidly with an unusually broad range of molecules under temperatures relevant to cold molecular clouds, making CH an important driver of molecular complexity in the interstellar medium. This review focuses on reactions of CH with polyatomic partners where low-temperature kinetic data are available (down to 23 K), drawing together information from theoretical studies, CRESU (Cinétique de Réaction en Ecoulement Supersonique Uniforme), and crossed molecular beam experiments. Trends in reaction rate coefficients as a function of temperature are surprisingly similar despite the differences in molecular reaction partner, with k ( T ) increasing with decreasing temperature before a small turnover in behavior near 50–70 K. This review evaluates k ( T ) and mechanistic trends in the context of a capture-controlled framework, highlighting where it breaks down and how observed trends in fitted rate parameters point toward predictive expressions for CH reactivity, while emphasizing the hydrocarbon and heteroatom-containing systems most in need of further study.
n71466527e8d1: The brain-gut-microbiome system is an integrated communication network linking the central nervous system, enteric nervous system, immune pathways, and intestinal microbiota. Increasing evidence indicates that dysregulation of this bidirectional signaling system contributes to both gastrointestinal and psychiatric disorders. Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), a disorder of gut–brain interaction, and major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently coexist and share multiple biological and environmental risk factors. Advances in microbiome science, neuroimaging, and multi-omics technologies have revealed that microbial metabolites, neuroimmune signaling, and stress-responsive neuroendocrine pathways influence neural circuits regulating mood, visceral perception, and gastrointestinal function. These interconnected mechanisms may explain the high comorbidity between IBS and MDD and suggest that both conditions arise from disturbances across overlapping biological systems. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge of genetic, neurobiological, and potential microbial contributors to IBS and depression, discuss emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the brain-gut-microbiome system, and highlight future directions for developing mechanistically informed treatment strategies.
n7ab72819eaa8: High-density direct current resistivity surveys play a crucial role in characterizing aquifer structures and groundwater contamination. However, the necessity of using multiple electrode arrays to achieve comprehensive subsurface imaging significantly prolongs field data acquisition, posing challenges to efficient hydrological investigations. This study validates an efficient approach that employs a single pseudo-dipole array to derive comprehensive datasets equivalent to those obtained from multiple standard arrays (e.g., Wenner α, β, γ). The pseudo-dipole configuration, which utilizes fixed reference electrodes positioned at the line ends, demonstrates vertical resolution comparable to that of conventional dipole arrays, while offering superior lateral resolution in our analysis. Numerical modeling and analytical solutions for homogeneous half-space, vertical contact, and multi-anomaly models confirmed that the pseudo-dipole array exhibits enhanced sensitivity to subsurface anomalies. Numerical experiments demonstrate that high-resolution apparent resistivity pseudosections and reliable inversion models, derived from transformed pseudo-dipole data, can effectively identify hydrological units. This method provides a time-efficient solution for detailed aquifer mapping and contamination plume monitoring, thereby enhancing the utility of electrical resistivity tomography in water resource management.
n932f61fcf733: A computer virus is a type of malware that, upon execution, can replicate itself by modifying other computer programs and inserting its code into them. This study develops a stochastic fractional-order delay differential equation model (SFDDE) to describe computer-virus dynamics by partitioning the system into uninfected S(t), latent infected L(t), and actively seizing V(t) computer populations. The model establishes the well-posedness of solutions, including existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness, and identifies two equilibria: the computer-virus-free equilibrium (CV-FE) and the computer-virus-present equilibrium (CV-PE). The basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method, followed by local and global stability analyses of the equilibrium points. A sensitivity analysis is performed to assess the influence of key parameters on virus transmission. Furthermore, a stochastic Non-Standard Finite Difference (NSFD) scheme is constructed to preserve the essential qualitative properties of the model, and its numerical performance is compared with the fractional Euler–Maruyama method using step-size refinement and quantitative error measures. The numerical experiments illustrate the effects of fractional memory, transmission delay, and stochastic perturbations on computer-virus dynamics. The results provide mathematical insight into computer-virus propagation and indicate the importance of reducing virus transmission and improving detection, removal, and recovery processes for effective cybersecurity management. The study demonstrates the usefulness of stochastic fractional-order delay modeling and structure-preserving numerical methods for analyzing complex computer-virus dynamics.
n8cbd6deb6f49: Purpose To evaluate the demographics, predisposing factors, microbiological profile, management, and outcomes of pediatric microbial keratitis in Eastern India, with particular emphasis on age-related differences. Materials and methods This prospective study included children with clinically diagnosed microbial keratitis between April 2024 and September 2025. Clinical, microbiological, nutritional, treatment, and outcome data were recorded. Children were categorized into two age groups: ≤ 5 years and >5 years for comparative analysis. Results Ninety-nine eyes of 86 children were analyzed. The mean age was 5.9 ± 4.8 years, and 42 of 86 children were aged ≤5 years. Bilateral keratitis was observed exclusively in children ≤5 years (p 5 years. Mean duration of presentation, ulcer size, and ulcer severity did not differ significantly between the two age groups, although perforation at presentation was more frequent in children >5 years. Fungal keratitis was significantly more common in children >5 years, whereas unidentified cases were more frequent in ≤5 years. Corneal ulcers resolved with medical therapy alone in 59.6% of eyes. Surgery was required in 40.4% of eyes overall, including 18.2% of eyes in children ≤5 years and 22.2% in children >5 years. At 3 months, corneal opacity was the most common outcome. Conclusion Pediatric microbial keratitis showed clear age-related differences. Younger children were more often affected by systemic and nutritional vulnerability with predominantly sterile or bacterial keratitis, whereas older children had more trauma-related and fungal disease. Early referral, improved nutritional support, and timely globe-preserving management may reduce visual loss. Conference presentation This research work has been selected for presentation at ARVO 2026, Denver, Colo. May 3 - 7
nfef38ce84e93: RNA structural changes caused by mis-splicing or transcription errors may affect antigenic features of cell surface proteins. They are especially noteworthy in the field of blood transfusion where the discrepancy between DNA-based molecular testing and serological blood typing are often encountered in clinical practice and lead to mismatched blood transfusion. In the Kidd (JK) blood group system weak Jka (Jk(a + w)) phenotype is usually missed in routine serological tests and causes delayed hemolytic transfusion reactions. However molecular bases underlying Jk(a + w) phenotype are still not clear although plentiful genomic DNA-based studies have been conducted. In this study, we used PacBio long-read sequencing to characterize open reading frame (ORF) region of SLC14A1 mRNA obtained from reticulocytes of 18 blood donors possessing JK*A alleles. Among them, 8 donors were determined as normal Jka antigen presentation and 10 donors showed Jk(a + w) phenotype in routine serological tests. We found that Jk(a + w) subjects demonstrated different exon combination patterns compared to those individuals presenting normal Jka antigens, implying the resulted SLC14A1 protein isoforms could make different contributions to the formation of the JK antigenicity. Moreover, exon skipping and exon inclusion that were frequently found in Jk(a + w) individuals could induce frameshift mutations. In addition, high levels of nucleotide insertions or deletions (indels) at 130A position were detected in the transcripts of Jk(a + w) individuals. Technical artifacts were examined using synthesized RNA templates and the results suggested that artifacts generated in reverse transcription and PCR amplification (RT-PCR) processes were unlikely the causes of these observations. All the results indicate that SLC14A1 RNA splicing and transcription fidelity play crucial roles in determining Jka antigen presentation.
n6cf2cfed6df4: Purpose Multi-room proton therapy centers face unique operational challenges related to shared beam delivery systems, extended treatment hours, and high clinical complexity. This study presents a structured framework of key performance indicators (KPIs) and reports longitudinal single-institution operational reference data from a multi-room proton therapy center to support operational assessment and continuous quality improvement. Methods and materials Operational KPIs were retrospectively evaluated for calendar year 2024 at a three-room proton therapy center utilizing pencil beam scanning. KPIs were categorized into three areas: beam performance, treatment planning and pre-treatment workflow, and treatment room operations. Beam performance metrics included site- and room-specific uptime and beam pauses. Treatment planning metrics quantified CT simulation–to–patient scheduling timelines with attribution to physician, dosimetry, and physics components. Treatment room operations metrics included appointment variance, slot utilization, and waiting-for-beam (WFB) time. Data were collected automatically using a commercial analytics platform integrating radio-frequency identification tracking and oncology information system. Metrics were analyzed longitudinally and stratified by treatment room, disease site, and workflow component. Results For calendar year 2024, aggregate site uptime was 95.3%, weighted according to clinical operating time across the three treatment rooms; individual room uptimes ranged from 91.8% to 97.2%. Beam pauses were frequent but brief, resulting in 2,238 minutes of cumulative lost treatment time across 2024, equivalent to approximately 0.5% of total clinical operating time. Annual mean treatment planning time was 8.5 business days, with physician-related activities contributing the greatest variability across disease sites. Monthly average appointment variance ranged from 5 to 11 minutes, with most treatments initiated within 10 minutes of scheduled time. Across 2024, slot utilization was stable, with 73% of fractions completed within scheduled slots. Mean overrun and underrun durations were modest, although P90 overrun durations exceeded 10 minutes throughout the year. Mean WFB times were low and consistent, ranging from 1.5 to 2.3 minutes. Conclusions This study presents a practical KPI framework and a single-institution operational reference data for multi-room proton therapy center. These metrics may support longitudinal monitoring, identification of workflow inefficiencies, data-driven decision-making, and future multi-institutional benchmarking efforts.
n16c544b98a89: To address the lack of a unified quantitative index for the ecological risk assessment of selenium (Se) in soils, the toxicity coefficient of Se was first determined based on Håkanson’s principles, and the spatial distribution and potential ecological risk of Se in surface soils across China were systematically evaluated. The results showed that the toxicity coefficient of Se was determined as 2. Based on the corrected background reference value, approximately 69.9% of the sampling sites were classified as low to moderate ecological risk, 24.4% as considerable risk, and 5.7% as high or very high risk. The elevated risk sites were predominantly confined to localized areas underlain by Se-rich strata, such as Enshi in Hubei Province and Ziyang in Shaanxi Province. A substantial consistency was observed between the potential ecological risk factor (Eri) and the geoaccumulation index (Igeo), with a quadratic weighted Kappa coefficient (κw) of 0.729, indicating that the two classification systems yield comparable results in terms of risk ranking. This study provides a preliminary screening benchmark for identifying areas that warrant further site-specific investigation.
n7a29eb3ca947: Norovirus, which is extremely contagious and has a significant impact on the gastrointestinal tract, has also been one of the main potential threats to health in the population. The use of fractional calculus has received much interest in the past few years with regard to the modeling of infectious diseases, especially because it allows modeling the memory and nonlocal processes in a dynamic system. In this study, a mathematical model is developed to investigate the transmission dynamics of norovirus. The proposed model consists of five epidemiological compartments: susceptible, exposed, infected, vaccinated, and recovered populations. The existence and uniqueness of the mathematical model are proven by a fixed-point theorem. The findings demonstrate that the sustainability of the disease-free equilibrium increases with a decrease in fractional order. In order to observe the effects of the fractional order on the dynamics of disease, numerical simulations are carried out based on the three-step Adams-Bashforth procedure, which supports the theoretical results with graphical illustrations. Moreover, the results are validated through the comparison with deep neural networks. The comprehensive nature of numerical simulations carried out at different fractional orders and transmission parameters indicates that the dynamics of fractional orders are effective in describing memory and heterogeneity of the disease transmission, which are characterized by classical integer-order models only to a limited extent. The results also indicate that the high coverage of vaccination and improvement in the effectiveness of treatment will greatly decrease the prevalence of infections. Further, the model has been demonstrated to be numerically stable and positive in real parameter disclosures. Altogether, this study provides a reliable mathematical approach and better understanding for analyzing disease dynamics and may be extended to other applications in epidemiology and related scientific fields.
n6e954072d36c: Composite dietary and lifestyle indices capture the combined effects of multiple health-related behaviours and may better reflect real-world cancer risk and survivorship than single exposures. This umbrella review aimed to evaluate and grade the strength of evidence for associations between adherence to composite dietary and lifestyle quality indices and endometrial cancer (EC) outcomes, including risk, EC-specific survival, overall survival, disease recurrence, quality of life, and new-onset cardiometabolic diseases. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library databases were systematically searched for relevant systematic reviews. Evidence was graded using prespecified umbrella review criteria. A total of 21 systematic reviews were included. Nine investigated diet quality (7 meta-analyses) and 12 investigated lifestyle exposure or interventions (8 meta-analyses). The outcomes assessed were EC risk (N = 14), all-cause or cancer-specific mortality (N = 5), recurrence (N = 4), overall or cancer-specific survival (N = 3), QoL (N = 5), and cardiometabolic events (N = 1). Following a Mediterranean diet was associated with 29% lower odds of EC (pooled OR = 0.71, 95% CI 0.51–0.98; class IV), whereas Western dietary patterns were associated with 20% higher odds of EC (pooled OR = 1.20, 95% CI 1.03–1.39; class IV). A combined healthy diet and lifestyle approach was associated with a 46% lower hazard of EC incidence (pooled HR = 0.54, 95% CI 0.42–0.71; class III), although heterogeneity was high. No significant associations were observed between lifestyle interventions and global or domain-specific quality of life (QoL) across follow-up durations ranging from 9 weeks to 12 months, irrespective of the validated assessment instruments used. Evidence remains limited regarding the associations between diet and lifestyle factors and EC recurrence, survival, mortality, and cardiometabolic outcomes. Our umbrella review identified suggestive (class III–IV) evidence for associations between healthy dietary patterns, particularly the Mediterranean diet, and combined healthy lifestyle approaches with lower EC incidence. Evidence remains insufficient or non‐significant for post-diagnosis outcomes, underscoring the need for further high-quality research.
ne19e1b814328: This scoping review aims to map and analyze the existing evidence on digital Patient Decision Aids (PtDAs) for cancer prevention targeting socially disadvantaged women. Cancer is a leading cause of premature mortality among women. Cancer prevention strategies can effectively reduce cancer incidence and mortality. Socially disadvantaged women face lower screening rates and higher mortality. Effective cancer prevention requires informed decision-making. One approach is the use of digital PtDAs. They represent a promising innovation for this population. However, their characteristics, development process, and evaluation for cancer prevention targeting this population remain underexplored. This scoping review will include digital PtDAs designed to meet the needs of socially disadvantaged women aged 18–75 in the context of cancer prevention and meeting the minimum criteria established by the International Patient Decision Aid Standards. We will include studies and sources covering quantitative and qualitative research, and gray literature. This scoping review will follow the JBI methodology for scoping reviews. A comprehensive three-step search will be conducted across MEDLINE, CINAHL, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane databases, Google Scholar and gray literature sources. All studies and sources available in any language will be considered. Citations will be imported into Rayyan for screening. Two independent reviewers will conduct study selection, data extraction, and analysis. Data will be summarized using tables and descriptive content analysis to identify characteristics, development processes, and evaluation methods of digital PtDAs. The review will be reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Findings will be submitted for publication in an international peer-reviewed journal and presented at national and international conferences focused on cancer prevention, shared decision-making, digital health or socially disadvantaged women. We will share findings with healthcare professionals, public health and cancer prevention stakeholders, and socially disadvantaged communities and their network. This protocol has been registered with the Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/f3428/).
n1f99a01a5a5b: Wild prey are shaped by predators long before they are caught. Fear alone suppresses reproduction, physical refuges reduce exposure, and many species strike back directly at their attackers, imposing real costs on the hunter. To investigate the combined effects of these behavioral mechanisms, we develop a Caputo fractional-order predator–prey model incorporating fear-induced reproductive suppression, proportional prey refuge, active anti-predator retaliation, a Holling type II functional response, and nonlinear saturation harvesting. The fractional memory order accounts for hereditary effects in ecological interactions, with the classical integer-order system recovered as a special case. Fundamental dynamical properties of the model, including non-negativity, uniform boundedness, and existence and uniqueness of solutions, are established. All biologically feasible equilibria are characterized, and local and global asymptotic stability conditions are derived using Matignon’s criterion and Lyapunov function techniques. The analysis further reveals that the coexistence equilibrium can lose stability through a Hopf bifurcation induced by the fractional memory order, and a critical threshold for the onset of this bifurcation is derived. Numerical evaluation of the first Lyapunov coefficient provides evidence that the bifurcation is supercritical, leading to the emergence of stable periodic oscillations. Applying Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle, we derive a bang–singular–bang optimal harvesting strategy that improves discounted net revenue while maintaining ecologically sustainable population levels. Numerical simulations support the theoretical results and illustrate the combined influence of fear, refuge, anti-predator behavior, harvesting, and memory on ecosystem dynamics. The findings demonstrate that the fractional memory order acts as an effective regulator of ecological stability, providing a biologically interpretable mechanism for controlling oscillatory behavior that has no counterpart in classical integer-order predator–prey models.
nce431fda5920: Background India has committed to achieving ‘Eliminate Tuberculosis (TB)’ by 2025. The Government of India issued guidelines regarding the crucial strategy of Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment in July 2021. Objectives To identify factors influencing tuberculosis preventive treatment program implementation and acceptance of tuberculosis preventive treatment. Methods We conducted the study in the Pune district from April to August 2024. It was a qualitative study using Focus Group Discussions (FGD) with Medical Officers (MO) and adult contacts of the index case, and In-depth Interviews (IDI) with senior health officers. We conducted eight FGDs with MOs and six with adult contacts, and conducted in-depth interviews with senior health officers. Data were transcribed, translated, and analyzed using MAXQDA. Results Eighty-six health/medical officers and 43 adult contacts participated in FGD and IDI. Some health officers have received training in tuberculosis but not in preventive treatment. Knowledge about tuberculosis preventive treatment and duration was minimal. Medical officers minimally briefed contacts. Stigma mainly from contacts perspectives, migration from health personnels perspectives and lack of awareness from both the groups emerged as important factors influencing screening and treatment of adult contacts. Very few underwent blood/ X-ray/ sputum testing, and fewer received treatment for varied durations. Medical officers knew only the isoniazid regimen, and interferon-gamma release assay testing was either unknown or unavailable. There is a shortage of trained human resources. The supply of diagnostic kits and medicines was disrupted. Health personnel and contacts recommended non-pharmacological measures such as mask use, cleanliness, and good nutrition. All officers perceived that elimination may linger until 2030. Training, counselling, community awareness, and multi-sectoral collaboration were strategies suggested by health officers. Conclusions Health personnel capacity building, strengthening infrastructure and logistics, multiple strategies to mitigate stigma, and multi-sectoral collaboration are needed to satisfactory implementation of TB preventive treatment.
n4bb4217e54c3: Background Chronic musculoskeletal pain is highly prevalent among older adults and is associated with disability, reduced physical activity, and decreased quality of life. Digital health interventions can improve access to care and support pain self-management. InControl is a user-centered web-based platform that combines exercise and pain science education. The aim of this pilot study is to assess the usability and acceptability of the InControl platform and the feasibility of the research methods. This will help inform methodological improvements in the design of a future randomized controlled trial. Methods A randomized, parallel-group, mixed-methods pilot study will be conducted with two groups: usual care group and the InControl intervention. Thirty-four participants aged 60 years or older with chronic musculoskeletal pain will be recruited at the Local Health Unit of Aveiro Region. The InControl intervention will last 8 weeks and will combine in-person sessions with remote interventions. Feasibility will be assessed using indicators of recruitment, retention, adherence, refusal, and dropout rates. Usability will be measured using the System Usability Scale, while acceptability and appropriateness will be assessed through a questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. Secondary outcomes will include pain, physical function, psychological factors, quality of life, and cognitive function. Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative thematic analysis. Discussion The findings will inform the design of a future large-scale randomized controlled trial and contribute to the development of more effective digital interventions tailored to the needs of older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Trial registration This study is registered on clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07774416 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07774416?tab=study), August 18, 2026.
n4b4a47f7176e: We extend the delayed reaction–diffusion SI model with nonlinear incidence proposed by Song et al. by replacing the fixed transmission lag with weak and strong gamma-distributed memory kernels. Because the model has no exposed compartment, the memory term is interpreted phenomenologically as a distributed timing of transmission-related effects of past infectious states rather than as an explicit latent-stage mechanism. Using the same parameter set adopted by Song et al., we show that the distributed-memory models have a stability structure that is qualitatively different from that of the discrete-delay model. For the spatially homogeneous mode, both gamma kernels exhibit a small stabilising spectral Hopf crossing at a mean memory time near 0.08. The discrete-delay model has a comparable small stabilising crossing but, in addition, a much larger destabilising crossing near τ=1.335. Consequently, at the nominal values 1.2 and 1.6 used in the reference simulations, the gamma models converge to the selected endemic equilibrium, whereas the discrete-delay model crosses into an oscillatory regime. The first spatial mode is different: for the gamma formulations its modal constant term is negative for every positive memory rate, so this mode is unstable for every positive mean-memory value. We therefore interpret this behavior as a memory-independent spatial-mode instability, distinct from both a memory-induced Hopf crossing and a classical Turing instability.
n6313663b8375: Groundwater chemistry reflects both natural and anthropogenic processes. In rapidly urbanizing areas where agricultural and construction land coexist, differences in shallow groundwater chemistry remain poorly understood. This study compared hydrochemical characteristics between agricultural and construction land-use types in the Jining National High-tech Zone, China, using geochemical diagrams, ion ratios, mineral saturation indices, and multivariate statistics. Groundwater in the study area was generally neutral to weakly alkaline, with pH 6.78–7.51 in agricultural samples and 7.19–7.47 in construction samples. Agricultural groundwater had higher mean TDS (797.28 vs 624.00 mg/L in construction groundwater) but lower variation, suggesting spatially uniform carbonate dissolution. Conversely, construction groundwater displayed higher mean Na+ concentrations (59.85 mg/L) and greater hydrochemical heterogeneity. After Holm correction, pH, TDS, total hardness, and Ca2+ differed significantly between the two land-use types (adjusted p 3-N, did not. The Cl- coefficient of variation exceeded 100% in construction areas, and NO3-N variability was elevated in agricultural areas. These patterns indicate mixed influences from silicate weathering, cation exchange, and localized anthropogenic inputs. Principal component analysis yielded three components: PC1 (44.62%) represented a mineralization gradient, PC2 (17.08%) reflected pH–alkalinity balance, and PC3 (14.17%) indicated silicate weathering versus carbonate dissolution. PC1 and PC2 scores differed significantly among land-use types (p = 0.007 and 0.009, respectively), but PC3 scores did not (p = 0.826). Overall, agricultural groundwater showed carbonate-dissolution dominance with pronounced nitrate enrichment (NO3-N 102.7%), while construction groundwater showed silicate-influenced, Na-Cl-coupled signatures with greater heterogeneity (Cl- 106.6%). These results link land-use differences to distinct shallow groundwater hydrochemical patterns, though such patterns may reflect combined influences of land use, hydrogeological setting, and aquifer lithology. The findings underscore the need for land-use-specific groundwater management in rapidly urbanizing agricultural-industrial regions and provide a baseline for future process-oriented research.
n5e2d6439f4eb: Dynamic changes in physiological oxygen levels are crucial for proper cortical brain development. In this context, oxygen is important not only for its role in energy metabolism but also as a signaling molecule. While much is already known about its most prominent signaling factor hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α, little is known about its functionally similar isoform HIF-2α during cortical development. Therefore, we utilized HIF-2α conditional knock-out mice (Emx1 and Nestin driven), which were kept under maternal hypoxia (10% pO2), physioxia (21% pO2), or hyperoxia (75% pO2) starting at E14.5 for 48 h and analyzed their cortical development by immunohistochemistry at E16.5. The analysis of newborn neurons (BrdU+) and cortical layer IV (Tbr1+), V (Ctip2+), and upper layer neurons (Satb2+) revealed clear effects of oxygen, with hyperoxia particularly increasing the number of Ctip2+/Tbr1- layer V neurons in E16.5 fetuses. However, neither the number of newborn neurons nor the number of layer-specific neurons was affected by HIF-2α CKO. Similarly, oxygen-related effects on neural stem cells (NSCs) and neuroprogenitor cells were not mediated by HIF-2α in E16.5 fetuses. Contributing, in vitro expansion and stem cell maintenance of NSCs were accelerated by physioxia (3% pO2) compared to hyperoxia (21% pO2), without involvement of HIF-2α under either condition. In conclusion, oxygen modulates cortical development, but HIF-2α does not mediate these effects. Thus, oxygen-related changes in neurogenesis and cortical morphology appear to be regulated via HIF-2α-independent mechanisms.
n73bb7590ec45: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings. Objective To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations. Methods A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026. Forty-four records were mapped. Thirty-three full comparative economic evaluations formed the primary synthesis; 11 partial or non-standard economic evidence records were retained as contextual evidence. The Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) checklist was applied retrospectively to assess reporting completeness, and a descriptive structured appraisal was used to examine methodological credibility across six health-economic domains. A Welte-informed assessment was used to examine target-context contextualization. Results The evidence base evolved from early static cohort models to dynamic transmission and individual-based approaches, while static models remained common in LMIC-focused standardized-tool analyses. The main drivers of variation were vaccine price, discounting, herd-immunity assumptions, cross-protection assumptions, and threshold selection. Reporting completeness varied and did not necessarily correspond to methodological credibility. Relevance to a study’s own decision setting did not imply that its ICER could be transferred to other countries. Eleven contextual records showed emerging policy questions around delivery costs, fiscal consequences, uptake, risk-benefit framing, and non-ICER-based decision support. Conclusion The economic value reported for HPV vaccination depends on the assumptions, comparators, vaccine prices, thresholds, and local screening contexts used in each evaluation rather than on the vaccine alone. Future evaluations should explicitly justify the choice of comparator, model structure, vaccine-price assumptions, discount rates, thresholds, uncertainty analysis, and transferability assumptions. Although formal cost-effectiveness analyses of single-dose HPV vaccination have begun to emerge, evidence remains limited, particularly regarding durability, waning, delivery feasibility, gender-neutral vaccination in LMICs, and country-specific evaluations in underrepresented regions.
n6c7ee5ac52d4: Colombia has become the principal host of Venezuelan migrants in Latin America, prompting a complex mix of solidarity, anxiety, and discrimination. This study offers a multidimensional analysis of Twitter (now X) discourse on Venezuelan migration in Colombia between 2014 and 2022, using natural language processing, geolocation inference, sentiment analysis, and manual annotation of derogatory terms. Drawing from 7.4 million posts, we examine how online discourse evolves across time, space, and language. While negative sentiment is pronounced in original tweets during periods of political and social unrest, our findings highlight that users tend to amplify neutral and positive messages—over 67% of retweets fall into these categories—suggesting an informal counterbalance to polarized discourse. Additionally, the analysis of the derogatory terms veneco and veneca reveals significant gendered patterns: the feminine form veneca appears more frequently in negative contexts, pointing to the gendered dimensions of xenophobic language. These results underscore the dual function of social media as a site of both stigmatization and resistance, offering insights into the emotional and cultural dimensions of migration discourse in Colombia’s digital public sphere.
n17455c3a0f8e: African American (AA) men experience disproportionately high prostate cancer incidence and mortality. Despite this disparity, current genomic repositories are predominantly derived from European populations, and studies using archived tissues are often limited by stromal contamination. We sought to characterize the high-resolution somatic mutational landscape of AA prostate cancer using a high-fidelity, patient-matched model system to identify population-specific drivers and therapeutic targets. We performed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on 10 matched pairs of primary cell cultures derived from prostate tumors and adjacent non-malignant tissues of AA patients. Our analyses revealed a complex, heterogeneous landscape characterized by significant genomic instability, including frequent chromothripsis and kataegis signatures. Mutation hotspots were concentrated on chromosomes 1, 2, 3, and X, with the highest mutation density on chromosome 17. Functionally impactful mutations were identified in critical oncogenic pathways, including chromatin remodeling (CHD1, ARID1A, ATRX, KDM6A) and DNA damage response (ATM, BRCA1/2, RAD51). Additionally, we identified potentially novel candidate mutations unique to this AA cohort, distinct from those in European-centric datasets. This study provides a foundational, patient-specific WGS dataset derived from African American prostate cancer cell models. The identification of high-frequency actionable alterations in epigenetic and DNA repair pathways highlights the utility of this renewable resource for developing tailored therapeutic interventions and addressing racial disparities in prostate cancer outcomes.
n515007e7ae08: Background Persons with albinism (PWAs) in Africa represent a vulnerable population facing social discrimination, severe health issues such as skin cancers, and precarious socioeconomic conditions. The objective of this study was to estimate the prevalence of albinism and map the distribution of persons with albinism in Togo in 2024. Method This cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted from November 2023 to October 2024 across all 39 health districts in Togo, and it included a telephone survey in which community health workers (CHWs) identified PWAs in their districts. CHWs were subsequently trained to perform onsite data collection using the Kobocollect application. Finally, the data were reviewed by national association representatives of PWAs to validate the data and address any gaps. The data were analysed using R software, while geographic mapping was performed with QGIS. Results A total of 1,521 PWAs were identified in Togo, which is a prevalence of 18.7 PWAs per 100,000 inhabitants (equivalent to 1/5,323; 95% CI [1/5,605; 1/5,065]). Sociodemographic and regional characteristics were available for 1,433 PWAs who consented to participate in this study and were included in the PWA database in Togo. Districts such as Kpélé, Danyi, and Amou presented the highest density of PWAs. The PWA population is predominantly young, with 62.7% under 25 years of age, and it has a slight female predominance (52.2%). Approximately 70.7% of PWAs reported daily exposure to the sun without adequate protection. Moreover, 61.6% had no regular income, and only 1.4% earned over 100 000 FCFA per month. Over 30% of PWAs experienced health issues related to albinism, yet only 37% had a medical follow-up record. Conclusion This first national study in Togo allowed us to estimate the prevalence of albinism in the country. The geographic distribution shows that PWAs are present throughout Togo, with concentrations in large cities. This type of research must continue to enable early identification and monitoring of PWAs to reduce the occurrence of serious health problems such as skin cancers.
n69150c0f830d: Objective To explore the effects and related mechanisms of a β-blocker combined with a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor (5-HT1AR) agonist on MI injuries in rats. Methods TTC/Evans blue, H&E, Masson, and TUNEL staining were used to assess infarction area, pathological damage, fibrosis, and apoptosis in myocardial tissue. The ELISA kits were used to detect IL-1β and IL-18 levels. The immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was used in conjunction with qRT-PCR and Western blot to determine IL-1β, IL-18, NLRP3, pro Caspase-1, cleaved Caspase-1, GSDMD-FL, and GSDMD-N expression levels. Results In myocardial tissue, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist effectively reduced infarction size, mitigated pathological injury, alleviated fibrosis, and prevented apoptosis. Meanwhile, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist downregulated IL-1β and IL-18 levels in serum and myocardial tissue. Notably, although it barely altered the expression of the pyroptosis precursor proteins pro Caspase‑1 and GSDMD‑FL, the combined therapy strongly suppressed the mRNA and protein levels of NLRP3, cleaved Caspase‑1, and GSDMD‑N, and reduced the ratios of pro Caspase‑1/cleaved Caspase‑1 and GSDMD-FL/GSDMD-N in myocardial tissue. Conclusion β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist relieves MI injuries by suppressing the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.
n8c9748cedb78: by Phil Y. Yao, Miles R. Fontenot, Casey A. Quinlan, Vikas N. O’Reilly-Shah Background Restoring intravascular volume in the face of hemorrhagic blood loss is a fundamental skill critical to the practice of anesthesiology. Predictors of fluid responsiveness in pediatric patients remain a challenge. Pulse pressure variation (PPV) is a valuable predictor of volume responsiveness in adults, but the utility in pediatric resuscitation remains controversial. Surgical correction of craniosynostosis occurs early in childhood and is commonly associated with significant, rapid blood loss intraoperatively. This study examines the relationship between blood product boluses with PPV and mean arterial pressure (MAP). Methods A retrospective, single center analysis of pediatric patients undergoing open cranial vault expansion over a four-year period was performed. Descriptive variables, blood product administrations, MAP, and PPV were extracted and analyzed using a linear mixed-effects model to characterize the association between blood product administration with MAP and PPV. To account for non-independence of repeated measures, the patient was modeled as a random effect with bolus events nested within the patient variable. Results A total of 798 bolus events from 111 patients met criteria. Patient ages ranged from 1–23 months (mean 10 months, SD 4.6 months). Transfusion of blood products was associated with increase in MAP by 1.60 mmHg [95% CI: 1.14, 2.06] and reduction in PPV by 0.82 percentage points [95% CI: 0.59, 1.06] (both p < 0.001). Notably, the magnitude of PPV reduction was dose-dependent: for each additional 10 mL/kg administered, post-bolus PPV decreased by an additional 0.4 percentage points [95% CI: 0.02, 0.07] (p = 0.002). In contrast, the MAP increase was not volume-dependent (interaction p = 0.918). Conclusion This retrospective analysis of pediatric craniosynostosis repair cases at a single institution suggests that PPV is associated with a dose-dependent response to volume resuscitation, while MAP showed a fixed-magnitude response. These preliminary findings warrant further study in multicenter validity.
n497ebeb75c68: Background Postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation is generally considered uncomplicated; however, patient-reported recovery outcomes in patients with cancer remain poorly characterized. The impact of patient-controlled sedation (PCS) on postoperative recovery has not been established. Objective To assess early postoperative recovery using the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) questionnaire in a prespecified substudy of the PACSPI-2 randomised clinical trial and to compare recovery between patients receiving local anaesthesia alone and those receiving local anaesthesia combined with patient-controlled sedation. Design and setting Prespecified substudy of a randomised, open-label clinical trial conducted at two Swedish anaesthesia departments. Patients Three hundred thirty-four adult patients with cancer. Interventions Local anaesthesia (LA) alone or LA combined with propofol-alfentanil PCS during SVP implantation. Main outcome measures Primary outcome was difference of postoperative total QoR-15 scores between groups. The primary endpoint of the parent PACSPI-2 trial was maximal intraprocedural pain. Results There was no overall difference in total postoperative QoR-15 scores between the treatment groups (P = 0.61). Total QoR-15 scores changed significantly over time (P < 0.001) in both groups. By postoperative day 1 (POD 1), mean QoR-15 scores had increased from baseline in both groups (mean difference 2.9 and 3.1, respectively; P = 0.02 for both), although these changes were below the published minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 6. Before discharge, the LA + PCS group showed its largest within-group improvement in QoR-15 (mean difference 5.6, P < 0.001), primarily driven by the “Emotional state” and “Psychological support” dimensions, however no significant between group differences were observed. Median pain scores on POD 1 were 3 (IQR 2–5) in both groups, with NRS ≥ 4 reported by 49% in the LA and 48% in the LA + PCS group. Conclusions Early postoperative recovery after subcutaneous venous port implantation was generally good and did not differ between the LA and LA + PCS group. A transient within-group improvement in emotional and psychological recovery domains was observed before discharge in the LA + PCS group. Pain on POD 1 remained common in both groups. These findings were based on secondary analyses and should therefore be considered exploratory. Trial registration European Union Clinical Trials Registry: EudraCT: 2021-003821-31, ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05688384
nb18e80a96a49: China possesses vast deep coalbed methane (CBM) resources, However, the dynamic evolution of reservoir pressure and permeability during the production process remains unclear, which restricts their efficient development. This study conducted to reveal the dynamic evolution of coal reservoir pressure and permeability under different production rates and its influence on the productivity of deep saturated CBM wells, so as to provide a theoretical basis for efficient development. Based on actual production data from deep saturated CBM vertical wells in the Shenfu Block, and considering positive and negative effects on coal reservoirs during drainage, this study utilizes reservoir pressure and permeability prediction models and derives from production dynamics to characterize the variations of reservoir pressure and permeability under different drainage rates, and analyzes their impacts on well productivity. The gas production curves of deep saturated CBM wells in the Shenfu Block can be classified into two types: decline type and stable type. The results show that the initial pressure drop rate is the key factor leading to productivity differentiation. Stable-type wells exhibit a lower initial pressure drop rate, a wider propagation range of reservoir pressure, and a permeability improvement of 5.4%, enabling sustained and efficient CBM production. In contrast, decline-type wells experience an excessively rapid initial pressure drop rate, resulting in slow reservoir pressure decline, limited permeability enhancement of only 0.9%, and a significant drop in productivity at later stages. To achieve high and stable production of deep saturated CBM wells, a strategy of “slow drainage and controlled pressure” should be adopted. It is recommended to control the bottomhole flowing pressure drop rate within 160 kPa/d during the initial production stage; appropriately increase the rate by 50–100 kPa/d during the gas production increase stage to promote gas desorption; and adjust it back to around 50 kPa/d during the later decline stage to maintain production.
nb390e98226c7: Post-wheat green manure incorporation can improve fallow-season resource use and crop productivity, but species-specific effects on soil greenhouse gas emissions and subsequent wheat yield remain unclear in spring wheat systems. A field experiment was conducted from 2022 to 2023 in the Yellow River Basin of Inner Mongolia, China, with five green manure species, namely common vetch, hairy vetch, sesbania, forage rapeseed, and forage oat, and a fallow control. Soil CO2, CH4, and N2O emissions, global warming potential (GWP), greenhouse gas intensity (GHGI), wheat growth, and grain yield were evaluated. The system acted as a source of CO2 and N2O and a sink for CH4. Compared with fallow, green manure incorporation numerically increased cumulative CO2 emissions by 7.29%−44.30% and GWP by 7.44%−39.64%, although treatment differences in GWP were not significant, with CO2 contributing more than 85% of total GWP. It also increased grain yield by 2.96%−11.95%. Despite the numerical increase in GWP, GHGI differed among species. Hairy vetch achieved the highest yield and lowest GHGI, common vetch reduced GHGI relative to fallow, and forage oat showed high yield with the lowest cumulative N2O emission. These results suggest that hairy vetch, common vetch, and forage oat are suitable for post-wheat incorporation in this region.
n01bb8f4967db: Stroboscopic light stimulation (SLS) reliably evokes geometric visual hallucinations and, in some contexts, altered-state experiences. Its increasing use in research, public, recreational and exploratory clinical settings creates a need for proportionate safety guidance. The main concern is a visually triggered seizure in a susceptible individual; reported non-epileptic responses include discomfort or distress. We combined a retrospective survey of safety practices and reported events across four laboratories, provider-reported operational data from two commercial SLS platforms, and a focused review of photosensitivity and sensory intolerance. Laboratory contributors reported 20 non-serious events that interrupted or modified participation, with no reported seizures or syncopal episodes. One commercial provider reported nine medically important or otherwise notable events across approximately 3.8 million sessions. The other reported five such events across more than 400,000 sessions. Because commercial adverse-event capture was passive and the laboratory protocols and monitoring procedures were heterogeneous, these figures cannot be used to estimate incidence or establish screening effectiveness. This synthesis informed a provisional Sussex Strobe Safety Screening Questionnaire (4SQ) and a layered, context-specific risk-management approach. The resulting framework distinguishes non-serious tolerability concerns from the principal medical risk of a visually provoked seizure in a susceptible individual, and supports conservative monitored familiarisation exposure, immediate stopping procedures and systematic adverse-event surveillance. The predictive performance of the 4SQ and the effectiveness of these precautions require formal evaluation; absolute SLS risk remains uncertain.
n2f9fa33bc822: The effects of homogeneously doped phases on the primary radiation damage of W-based targets were investigated by the Monte Carlo method in this paper. The results show that introducing homogeneously doped phases into W effectively reduces the energy localization of deuterium ions within the targets. Meanwhile, Under 100 keV deuterium ion irradiation, the ballistic distribution, the number of displacement collisions, and the vacancies of deuterium ions in homogeneously doped W targets are all lower than those in pure W. And longitudinal analysis along the depth of all homogeneously doped specimens confirms that homogeneously TiC-doped W offers the strongest suppression of primary radiation damage in the near-surface region. Under 200 keV deuterium ion irradiation, the governing effects of various dopant species and dopant contents on primary radiation damage are summarized as follows: increasing dopant content leads to an approximately linear reduction in vacancies, with Ti dopant showing the strongest vacancy inhibition effect, while the ion range rises linearly and W–TiC possesses the most significant range variation. Large sampling fluctuations of sputtering yield make it an unreliable indicator for evaluating doping performance. Overall, dopants effectively mitigate primary irradiation damage in tungsten. These volume-averaged primary irradiation damage results derived from SRIM simulation are expected to offer reference insights into improving the irradiation tolerance of W by optimizing their compositional design, while microstructural interface effects need further multi-scale modeling for quantitative analysis.
nbb2aedffbd40: Background Population-based evidence on Breast Cancer (BC) survival and disease burden in Tunisia remains limited. This study aimed to describe BC survival and temporal trends, quantify the BC burden, and assess the impact of early diagnosis on survival and burden. Methods We conducted a descriptive population-based cohort study of women diagnosed with BC in Monastir between 2002 and 2014, with follow-up through January 2022. Overall survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods, and factors associated with mortality were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. BC burden was quantified using disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), comprising years of life lost (YLLs) and years lived with disability (YLDs). Relative risks (RRs) and related measures were used to assess the association between stage at diagnosis and mortality. Results Among 1,075 incident BC cases identified between 2002 and 2014, 21.4% were diagnosed at stage IV. By 2022, vital status information was available for 959 women. The crude and age-standardized mortality rates were 11.9 (95% CI, 8.5–15.4) and 12.5 (95% CI, 8.9–16.0) per 100,000 WY, respectively. Median survival was 187 months (95% CI, 163.7–210.2), reaching 226 months among women diagnosed at stages 0–I. Three-, five-, and ten-year survival rates were 77.0%, 70.0%, and 45.2%, respectively. Ten-year relative survival showed a significant upward trend among women aged 30–64 years, corresponding to the target population of the national BC early detection program (APC, 5.37%; 95% CI, 2.03–8.82; p = 0.005). The total BC burden was 10,665.4 DALYs, including 10,362 YLLs (97.3%). Median DALYs per patient was 28.0 years (IQR, 13.74–36.95). Diagnosis at stages 0–II was associated with a 22% reduction in ten-year mortality (RR, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67–0.91), with an NND of 9. Diagnosing 61 women at stages 0–II rather than III–IV would avoid one DALY. Conclusion The significant upward trend in ten-year survival among women targeted by the national BC early detection program, together with the avoidance of one DALY per 61 women diagnosed at stages 0–II rather than III–IV, supports continued investment in early detection and BC control in Tunisia.
n6bf72b0566ec: Background Violence against LGBTIQA+ individuals is not limited to discrete acts of aggression. It also constitutes a territorial ecology that unevenly distributes habitability, safety, and recognition. This study examines how the statement “Talca is not Santiago” works as more than a comment on city size: it names a moral geography where reputation, social surveillance, and uneven access to infrastructure produce distinct thresholds of visibility, risk, and agency. Methods We used Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA) following Braun and Clarke to analyze a subcorpus of seven individual interviews and one focus group (n = 7) conducted in Talca and one focus group (n = 5) conducted in Santiago, drawn from a broader research project according to predefined criteria (density of territorial references and representation of both study sites). Reporting follows COREQ guidelines (S1 Checklist). We recruited participants through LGBTIQA+ organizations and social networks; participants self-identified with non-hegemonic sexual-gender identities, were over 18, and reported subjective experiences of violence. The analytical sample is composed predominantly of young (19–35 years) university-educated participants, with representation of cisgender, transmasculine, and non-binary identities and no trans women. We calibrate the scope of our conclusions accordingly. Results We constructed three themes: (1) Infrastructure of possibility—LGBTIQA+ life becomes practicable or precarious depending on available circuits of information, networks, and spaces; (2) Surveillance and reputation—in medium-sized cities and rural environments, social legibility intensifies daily control and shrinks the margin to maneuver, which also affects the possibility of leaving violent relationships; (3) Mobility and education as partial territorial rupture—moving for studies and traveling through urban circuits reconfigures future horizons without erasing access asymmetries. Conclusions Within the scope of a young, predominantly cisgender, university-educated sample, territorial scale operates as a constitutive condition of violence and survival, not as a backdrop. Interventions on LGBTIQA+ violence therefore need to address territorial conditions: connectivity, information circulation, community spaces, and confidentiality safeguards adapted to medium-sized cities and ruralities.
n6b4c8a04280b: by Mike K. P. So, Jenny T. Y. Tsang, Lupe S. H. Chan, Jacky N. L. Chan, Agnes Tiwari, Amanda M. Y. Chu Background Depression is a prevalent mental health condition that significantly affects individuals’ well-being and daily functioning, making early depressive symptom detection crucial. Objectives This study explores the potential of advancing speech analytics with dimensional sentiment analysis, using valence and arousal scoring to enhance depressive symptom detection in family caregivers. Methods We recruited 116 family caregivers and assessed their depression levels using the Beck Depression Inventory-II. Participants provided verbal responses to 12 open-ended questions related to family resilience. The extracted words from the responses were analyzed for sentiment using the Chinese Valence-Arousal Words dictionary to determine their valence and arousal ratings. For each participant, we computed various summary statistics (e.g., mean, variance, quantiles) and frequency-domain statistics (e.g., spectral entropy, dominant frequency components) of valence and arousal distributions. These features were then used as predictors in nine different machine learning models evaluated under repeated 5-fold nested cross-validation with cost-sensitive cutoff selection, enabling robust classification of depression levels while prioritizing the identification of true positive cases. Results Our analysis showed that participants with higher depressive symptoms used words with more extreme valence and arousal scores than those with lower depressive symptoms. The models demonstrated strong predictive utility of these emotional dimensions: the quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA) model achieved an out-of-sample sensitivity of 0.725, a specificity of 0.563, and an AUC of 0.7. These findings support that valence and arousal analysis provides meaningful discriminative power for identifying depressive symptoms. Importantly, the high sensitivity achieved by these models ensures that individuals with elevated symptoms are more reliably detected, thereby reducing the risk of missed cases. Overall, the results suggest strong potential for automated depressive symptom detection based on emotional signal analysis, with cost-sensitive optimization reducing false negatives while maintaining clinically relevant specificity. Conclusions This study offers proof-of-concept evidence that emotional sentiment analysis of speech using valence and arousal scoring can capture linguistic markers associated with depressive symptoms among family caregivers. With further refinement and validation, this approach lays an important foundation for the development of more robust machine learning models and ultimately contributes to non-intrusive mental health screening tools.
n27a8e44e4557: by Brian T. Hamel, Jan E. Leighley, Jonathan Nagler Voters in American congressional midterm elections are widely viewed as demographically less representative than those in presidential elections – older, whiter, wealthier, and more educated. Using Current Population Survey data from 1994 through 2024 as well as voter-file data, we test this conventional wisdom and show that it is partly right but too broad. The key difference between midterm and presidential electorates is age: midterms sharply underrepresent young citizens and overrepresent older citizens compared to presidential elections, while differences between the elections by race, income, and education are much smaller. Midterm voters are, above all, older voters.
na0325eb023b8: Theropod dinosaur remains from the Barremian (Lower Cretaceous) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK, are rare and often fragmentary. Here, we present a previously undescribed braincase from this formation that represents a new coelurosaurian, Invictibellatrix amberina gen. et sp. nov. Phylogenetic analysis and comparative anatomy indicate that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods from this stratigraphic unit. Theropod braincases are often regarded as morphologically and phylogenetically conservative, but we demonstrate that neurocranial characters provide essential data that can help clarify the phylogenetic relationships of theropods. The sub-circular occipital condyle, sub-oval foramen magnum and presence of a sagittal nuchal crest indicate that Invictibellatrix is referable to Megaraptora, with phylogenetic analyses recovering it as an early-diverging member of this clade, within a paraphyletic array of Eurasian taxa. Incorporation of Invictibellatrix into a biogeographical analysis suggests that non-megaraptorid megaraptorans likely had a cosmopolitan distribution in the Early Cretaceous, and that the absence of megaraptorans in the Late Cretaceous of Laurasia is best explained by regional extinction. The recognition of this new genus increases our knowledge of Early Cretaceous European coelurosaurian diversity, which now includes tyrannosauroids, maniraptoriforms and megaraptorans.
n759fb0df395b: In past decades, conceptual analysis has established that evolution by natural selection (ENS) can occur without reproduction (Bouchard 2008 Philos. Sci. 75, 560–570 (doi:10.1086/594507); Papale, 2021 Synthese 198, 10 429–10 455 (doi:10.1007/s11229-020-02729-6)). The aim of this paper is to provide a computational proof of concept for this theoretical advance and to start assessing some of its conceptual upshots. To do so, we designed an agent-based model that introduces and defends a niche construction-based account of ENS without reproduction (ENSwR, pronounced like ‘answer’). Our results provide a computationally tractable proof of concept for ENSwR and a basis to reflect on some of its conceptual implications for debates regarding the origins of life. First, conceptual analysis suggests that ENSwR provides a novel explanatory framework that supports origins of life theories in which autocatalytic sets (ACSs) of chemical reactions play a central role (Xavier, Kauffman 2022 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 380, 20210244 (doi:10.1098/rsta.2021.0244)). Second, through a discussion of the hydrothermal vent theory for the origins of life, we show that ENSwR will contribute to explaining the evolutionary origins of reproduction.
n9e969a1692e5: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. Records from Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar within a documented 2020–2025 review window were screened using explicit eligibility criteria and assessed with an evidence-completeness rubric covering key reporting domains for cross-study comparison. The final corpus comprised 204 studies across photocatalytic/photo-assisted, electrochemical/electro-Fenton, Fenton-type, sulfate-radical, ozone-based, sonochemical, plasma-assisted and hybrid systems. Parent 2,4-D removal or analytical confirmation was reported in 202 studies, while carbon-based mineralization or organic-load evidence was reported in 116, transformation products in 95, residual toxicity in 27, real-water validation in 67 and reactor-scale or transferability information in 37. These patterns show stronger evidence for parent-compound disappearance than for treatment completeness, residual hazard and transferability. No AOP family was universally superior across removal, mineralization, toxicity reduction, matrix robustness, energy demand, durability and scale readiness. Future studies should standardize reporting of mineralization, transformation products, toxicity, energy boundaries, leaching, durability and reactor descriptors.
nfbe90dfa6f81: This study investigated the recovery and nanoliposomal formulation of anthocyanin-rich extracts from black rice using choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). Choline chloride/1,2-propanediol (DES2) produced the highest anthocyanin content, 85.5 ± 3.4 mg l−1, after optimization, compared with 25.7 ± 2.1 mg l−1 obtained by conventional ethanol extraction. High-resolution QTOF-MS/MS enabled the tentative assignment of cyanidin 3-O-hexoside-type and peonidin 3-O-hexoside-type compounds based on accurate precursor masses and characteristic product ions; authentic-standard confirmation was not performed. The DES2 extract showed greater apparent thermal stability than the control extract, with estimated half-lives of 30.0 and 16.0 days, respectively, at 45°C. Anti-oxidant activity was observed in DPPH and ABTS assays, with IC50 values of 0.19 ± 0.06 and 0.16 ± 0.08 mg ml−1, respectively. Preliminary antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli was detected under the tested agar-diffusion conditions, whereas activity against Staphylococcus aureus was limited. Nanoliposomal encapsulation achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 73.8 ± 4.3%, a Z-average diameter of 201.3 nm and 89.83 ± 0.65% anthocyanin retention after 28 days at 4°C. The formulation produced a larger inhibition zone against E. coli than the free extract under the assay conditions. These findings support further investigation, although release kinetics, pharmaceutical efficacy and complete-process sustainability remain unestablished.
n58801560c7be: After the leakage of a buried pipeline, the overlying soil structure deforms under the high-speed impact of escaping gas, influencing both leakage and diffusion behaviours. This deformation typically appears as a soil cavity above the leakage port, especially in medium- and low-pressure conditions. In this study, the formation process of soil cavities is investigated using CFD–DEM coupled numerical simulations. The control variable method is applied to examine how different conditions affect cavity size and gas diffusion, and the sensitivity between cavity characteristics and leakage behaviour is analysed. Results show that the leaked gas forms a high-velocity zone near the leakage port, generating negative pressure in the surrounding area. Soil cavities generally form and stabilize within 0.1 s under gas impact. Soil particle size and porosity significantly influence the cavity formation time by altering the pore structure and total pore volume. The average sensitivity coefficients of the maximum cavity width to gas leakage velocity and the highest dangerous range (HDR) are 5.71 and 18.78, respectively, indicating that larger cavity widths correspond to higher leakage velocities and greater HDR. Therefore, the maximum cavity width serves as the most appropriate indicator for evaluating soil cavities caused by buried gas pipeline leakage.
n22e69b0de952: Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. Additionally, understanding whether shared evolutionary history influences urban tolerance could shed light on its evolutionary origins and reveal the extent to which urban landscapes filter out entire taxonomic clades, homogenizing biodiversity. Here, we assessed the relationship between urban tolerance and eight different life history and ecological traits for 431 North American bird species. We found that birds with higher urban tolerance are longer-lived, smaller-bodied, and more likely to be sedentary or mixed migrants than birds with lower urban tolerance. Birds with higher urban tolerance also have broader environmental tolerance, based on breeding range size and estimates of range-wide variation in precipitation, consistent with their greater likelihood of being habitat generalists. We additionally detected a phylogenetic signal for urban tolerance, with several clades sharing similar urban tolerance measures. Our study identifies several mechanisms that likely underlie species differences in urban tolerance and demonstrates how urban areas can filter bird species based on their life history and ecological traits.
n16111fed2f84: Many animals defend themselves with toxic chemicals and use multimodal warning displays involving odours and bright colours to advertise their toxicity. Yet, how coloration and odour interact and why they so often evolve together is not well understood. Recent work in jumping spiders has shown that defensive odours from three chemically defended bugs (Order Hemiptera: Acanthocephala femorata, Mormidea sp. and Leptoglossus phyllopus) increase a foraging aversion to red prey. Here, we ask whether these odours also increase avoidance of another visual warning: high-contrast stripes. Jumping spiders (Habronattus trimaculatus) were given choices between pattern-manipulated termites (solid white and black-and-white striped) in the presence or absence of a defensive odour from one of the aforementioned bug species. We predicted that any aversion to stripes would be stronger when odour was present. Surprisingly, we found no effect of any bug odour on the spiders’ aversions to stripes. Interestingly, these odours that so strongly and consistently trigger aversion to red do not have the same effect on stripes. This highlights the different ways that odours and coloration can interact (or not) to influence predators, providing insight into the diversity of aposematic displays in nature.
n74f0a6ed12d1: Parent–offspring communication depends on offspring signals that help parents assess need and allocate care.
